Introduction and meaning
Defines cruelty for s. 85: wilful conduct likely to drive the woman to suicide or cause grave injury, or harassment to coerce dowry. Charge 85, define with 86. BNS restatement of IPC 498A Expl.. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 86 is the rule on “Cruelty defined”. The section provides that for the purposes of section 85, “cruelty” means—. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 86 exists so that “Cruelty defined” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.

The provision in detail
86. For the purposes of section 85, “cruelty” means—

(a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or

(b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand

Definitions and key terms

examples.title: Example 1 — simple (teaching example)
examples.body: A short everyday fact pattern is tested against “Cruelty defined”. Name BNS s. 86, list the ingredients, and say which facts match. This is a teaching example — the statute does not print a numbered illustration under this heading.

examples.title: Example 2 — practical application / distinction (teaching example)
examples.body: Change one ingredient so that BNS s. 86 fails. A complex problem or motion often hinges on this subtle missing ingredient. State the failure expressly. Label this as an example, never as a reported case.

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 86 (Cruelty defined) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 86 (Cruelty defined), Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) For the purposes of section 85, “cruelty” means—
   (2) (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or
   (3) (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 86 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 86 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

rows.right: Read the neighbour’s title on its own page before you write.

rows.left: For the purposes of section 85, “cruelty” means—
rows.right: Different ingredients — do not paste this section’s test onto the neighbour.

rows.left: Citing a neighbour as if it were s. 86.
rows.right: Citing s. 86 where the neighbour actually applies.

misconceptions.trap: Writing only the section number and title without analyzing ingredients or case ratio.
misconceptions.correction: An authoritative note defines the concept, lists ingredients, uses an illustration, states explanations/exceptions, applies the test, and concludes with BNS s. 86.

misconceptions.trap: Copying a statutory illustration without mapping it to an ingredient.
misconceptions.correction: Quote the illustration, then write which ingredient it proves or which ingredient is missing. Mapping is the core evidentiary link.

misconceptions.trap: Giving a one-line summary or shortened explanation of the provision.
misconceptions.correction: Authoritative chamber practice and judicial papers require a complete answer. The analysis on this page is written at full length for that reason.

Comprehensive Written Submissions. Deepen the doctrinal synthesis with four foundational layers.

Layer 1 — Place the section in the Chapter. Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.. Show why this heading sits where it sits.

Layer 2 — Work a second, slightly harder hypothetical. Change one ingredient and show why the section then fails.

Layer 3 — Distinction. Contrast BNS s. 86 with BNS s. 85. Write a short table in prose: meaning, ingredients, stage of the case, consequence. Confusion of neighbouring sections is the most common reason arguments collapse under judicial scrutiny.



Layer 5 — Application and current-law close. Apply the test to the problem facts in IRAC form (Issue, Rule, Application, Conclusion). Close with: “The governing citation on or after 1 July 2024 is BNS s. 86.”

revisionPoints: First ingredient: For the purposes of section 85, “cruelty” means—
No printed illustration — prepare an original labelled example.

For offences on or after 1 July 2024, the correct citation is BNS s. 86 — Cruelty defined. Older books and judgments may still print a historical number (498A Expl.). Convert it. Write the BNS number in a current answer. Do not treat the old number as if it were still the law.
